content:
Hi all, I’ve formalized the PBR theorem in PhyslibAlpha (PhyslibAlpha/QuantumMechanics/Foundations/: OntologicalModel, PBR/{Phases, QubitFrame, Measurement, Theorem}), and I would quite like to work towards getting it into Physlib.

Two (quick) questions about the current state of the PBR formalisation:

  1. Is PBR something you’d want in Physlib?
  2. OntologicalModel, Measurement and Theorem depend on the Alpha ProbabilisticTheory framework (Measurement.Finite, CStarAlgebra.OrderUnit, OrthonormalMeasurement) and on FiniteTarget.ProductState. Counting everything those import, that’s about 59 Alpha files. Is moving that framework into Physlib planned? Or should I restate the theorem on top of something already outside Alpha, e.g. QuantumInfo’s MState/POVM?

Phases and QubitFrame only depend on Mathlib and Physlib, so I could move those first if that’s useful.

The 5 PRs in this formalisation:

  1. #1904 (product vectors, phase invariance of vector states, Measurement.ofOrthonormal)
  2. #1914 (ontological models, ψ-ontic models, preparation independence)
  3. #1915 (Walsh characters, choice of PBR phases)
  4. #1916 (qubit frame of 2 unit vectors)
  5. #1917 (PBR theorem)
Im actively working on getting ProbabilisticTheory into Physlib. CStarAlgebra is definitely coming soon.

I think eventually having the PBR theorem in Physlib would be good.

There is one thing you can do to help get things into Physlib quicker: Look at the review comments that tend to go on PRs in Physlib, and the sorts of things which are asked for. Make sure that the code you added to PhyslibAlpha satisfies these conditions.

Looking towards those files which as you say already only depend on Physlib and Mathlib is a good candidate.

Thanks, I've updated my PRs to make the changes - 1 to 3 should be able to be merged into Physlib proper, but 4 onwards depend on ProbabilisticTheory and CStarAlgebra so we'll see if there are any workarounds for those 2. Also, I've split the Walsh and PBR phase PR into 2: #1920 (Walsh) and #1917 (PBR phases) - any review of #1914 onwards would be greatly appreciated!
